newsitem.title: USA: Casey's Q3 margins hurt by higher prices.
newsitem.headline: Casey's Q3 margins hurt by higher prices.

text.p: Casey's General Stores Inc, reporting lower earnings for the January 31 third quarter, said because of higher wholesale prices gasoline margins were down an average of 20.3 percent for the quarter.
The retail price that customers pay for a gallon of gasoline was up 18.7 percent.
"We also were up against a year-ago quarter when gasoline margins were exceptionally strong," said chairman Donald Lamberti in a statement.
"The good news is we've seen a significant improvement in wholesale gasoline prices over the past few weeks," Lamberti added.

He said Casey's remains on target to open 70 new stores in the current fiscal year. It ended the third quarter with 1,040 stores, an increase of 61 over the same time a year ago. This includes 870 corporate-owned stores and 170 franchise outlets.
Earlier Tuesday, Casey's reported third-quarter earnings of $0.21 per share compared to $0.26 per share a year ago. Sales rose 22.8 percent to $272.1 million.
